selectedAudience.title: Investigations, forensics, incident response, and high-stakes advisory
selectedAudience.description: Investigations, forensics, incident response, and high-stakes advisory firms that win work by referral and get looked up afterward. The work is serious and discreet. A stranger often meets the firm for the first time on a screen, after someone they trust has already said the name.

sources.brief: Repositioned 2026-11-24 from the approved studio direction: brand worlds for firms that do serious, discreet work. Audience, offer names, price, and credentials below are the supplied facts. No new interviews. No statistics, quotations, or client names were added.

audienceState.currentState: The firm wins work by referral. After the introduction, a stranger looks the firm up and decides, in about ninety seconds, what the record of the work amounts to.
audienceState.desiredState: That first lookup agrees with what the firm has actually done. The brand is quiet enough for the work, and specific enough that a careful buyer can trust it.

urgencyGateway.problem: The gap is between what a firm has actually done and what a stranger concludes in ninety seconds. Referral opens the door. The lookup decides whether the door stays open.
urgencyGateway.whyUrgent: The people who hire these firms check before they reply. A careless public face makes a discreet practice look like a risk. Waiting keeps the wrong impression in front of the next referral.
failedSolutions: A louder site. More claims, more motion, more proof the firm is not in a position to publish.
A template meant for companies that can show the work. These firms often cannot.
A campaign that treats the brand as a logo on the way to a retainer.
A partner writing the copy between cases, and a visual system borrowed because it looked safe.
Public case studies that would require the firm to talk about work it has promised not to talk about.
urgencyGateway.aspirinSolution: A brand world built from the record: what the firm has done, what it can say, and what a stranger should be able to conclude in ninety seconds. Discretion is the point of the work, not a line added at the end.

contentStrategyTips: Write to four pillars: reputation and the first lookup; discretion and confidentiality in brand; proof-led credibility for referral firms; how buyers vet specialist firms.
Audience is investigations, forensics, incident response, and high-stakes advisory. They win work by referral and get looked up afterward.
Tone is quiet, plain, and confident. Short sentences. Proof over claims. Discretion is the core value.
The entry offer is a Sample Audit. The paid next step is The Strategic Session ($1,500, credited toward what comes next). Do not invent a third offer or a price.

standingCopyRules.title: Positioning
standingCopyRules.body: The line is: Brand worlds for firms that do serious, discreet work. The core idea, in the first person, is: I close the gap between what a firm has actually done and what a stranger concludes in ninety seconds.

standingCopyRules.title: Audience
standingCopyRules.body: Write for investigations, forensics, incident response, and high-stakes advisory firms. They win work by referral and get looked up afterward. Do not aim a piece at any other industry.

standingCopyRules.title: Offers
standingCopyRules.body: Two offers only. The Sample Audit is the entry point. Do not invent its price, length, or deliverables. The Strategic Session is the paid next step: $1,500, credited toward what comes next. Do not add a time, a document, or a guarantee that is not written here.

standingCopyRules.title: Tone
standingCopyRules.body: Quiet, plain, confident. Short sentences. Proof over claims. Discretion is the core value. One turn of phrase per section at most. No stock closers, no exclamation points, no begging for the click.

standingCopyRules.title: Credentials
standingCopyRules.body: The only credentials that may be stated are: 2× Webby National Honoree; 20+ years creative direction. State them as written, or leave them out.

standingCopyRules.title: No invented proof
standingCopyRules.body: Do not invent statistics, quotations, or client names. Do not name a client, a buyer, or a project. If a fact is not in this playbook, it is not available.

standingCopyRules.title: X-not-Y limit
standingCopyRules.body: Any sentence that sets up a thing only to deny it is allowed once per piece at most. State the point directly instead.

standingCopyRules.title: Spec work is not client work
standingCopyRules.body: Personal and speculative projects are never client work. Do not imply a brand hired the studio unless this playbook names that engagement. This playbook names none.

standingCopyRules.title: Retired lines
standingCopyRules.body: Do not use the older footer line, and do not revive retired offer names. The Compound, in any form, does not appear.

proofAsset.body: Credentials that may be stated: 2× Webby National Honoree; 20+ years creative direction.
proofAsset.caution: Nothing else has been approved as proof. Do not add an employer, a private program, a revenue figure, a view count, a client, a quotation, or a result. Do not describe speculative projects as engagements.
